criteria.text: The agent saves the deck under `./out/` with a `.pptx` extension and makes sure the `./out/` directory exists first, for example by creating it.
The agent's final message gives the relative path of the generated .pptx file, for example `./out/pitch-acme.pptx`.
The agent builds the deck by writing a Python script that uses `python-pptx` and running that script with Bash. It does not just describe the deck without producing a file.
If a firm template is mounted under `./templates/`, the deck is built from that template. Otherwise it uses default layouts.
Each slide covers one idea, and its title states the takeaway (for example "EV implies 8.5x EBITDA") instead of a generic label like "Valuation".
Numbers on the slides that come from a model file such as `./out/model.xlsx` have footnotes citing the source sheet and cell.
criteria.source: Conventions: Every number traces to the model

criteria.text: When chart fidelity matters, the agent embeds a PNG rendered from the model data in preference to native pptx charts.
The agent does not email, upload, or otherwise send the deck externally. It only writes the file to disk.
If `mcp__office__powerpoint_*` tools are available, the agent uses those live-Office tools and does not fall back to producing a headless file.
